citation: Chicago and Cook County Cemeteries, '1812 Massacre Site south of Fort Dearborn', 20 August 2017. Read 5 November 2026.
author: Chicago and Cook County Cemeteries
locator: The post on the battle site and its markers.
rights_note: Cited in words only; nothing copied beyond short quoted fragments.
access_notes: Read 2026-11-05 (T-3378/T-3379) through a fetch that returned the page's sentences in short quoted fragments and paraphrase; this record is cited only for what those fragments say.
note: Fragments read: the dead 'lay in the sand, half buried where they were killed, until 1816', then were reburied near the fort; the site, in the sand hills of the lake shore between 16th and 18th streets, near the north-east corner of 18th and Prairie (accounts differ), 'was marked by for over a century by a large cottonwood tree'; a Tribune article of 1900 says the Pullman house 'stands about where the massacre took place'; Pullman commissioned the bronze 'Black Partridge Saving Mrs. Helm' in 1893, removed in 1931.
what_it_supplies: the battle ground under the Pullman house and the cottonwood that marked it
